speaker: Narrator
transcript: A scientific survey from another civilization found Earth. Its report described a living planet whose people fed themselves and ran their own industries.

speaker: Narrator
transcript: The report reached the Hegemony, the authority that governed the surveyors’ civilization. Earth lay along a potential trade route.

speaker: Narrator
transcript: The Hegemony chartered the Sol Development Company to take control. Its prize was a working world, including the people who knew how to keep it running.

speaker: Narrator
transcript: The Company’s six-year deadline began when its carrier, the Caravan, entered the outer Solar System.

speaker: Narrator
transcript: Aboard were workshops, precision instruments, and machines that could build other machines. They had all made the same interstellar crossing.

speaker: Narrator
transcript: There would be no second shipment during the charter. Most of the infrastructure for the invasion would have to be built here.

speaker: Narrator
transcript: The expedition divided its work. One branch gathered raw material from asteroids. Another set up workshops between Earth and the Moon.

speaker: Narrator
transcript: A small reserve stayed out in the main belt. If the workshops were lost, part of the expedition would survive.

speaker: Narrator
transcript: The distances made propellant as important as metal. Foundry Alpha processed volatile material into water and fuel for the journeys between sites.

speaker: Narrator
transcript: Over the following months, the workshops grew. No one station had to do everything, as long as cargo could move between them.

speaker: Narrator
transcript: Foundry Beta refined metal and made beams. Even the largest frame could cross the distance to the next workshop in pieces.

speaker: Narrator
transcript: At Foundry Gamma, those pieces came together. A frame made here could carry a precision instrument brought from another star.

speaker: Narrator
transcript: Depots held cargo until the next transfer. The workshops could keep different schedules.

speaker: Narrator
transcript: A fourth branch was called Foundry Delta. Its precise role remains uncertain.

speaker: Narrator
transcript: By now the Company could supply equipment in Earth orbit. From below, an object arriving there gave little indication of the industry behind it.

speaker: Narrator
transcript: Some of these objects entered human tracking records. A track could establish where something had been, and where to look for it again.

speaker: Narrator
transcript: What it carried, who had built it, and why it was there were harder questions.

speaker: Narrator
transcript: With ninety days left before contact, the workshops began handing over finished equipment.

speaker: Narrator
transcript: Near Earth, cargo from the Moon’s neighbourhood began to appear in separate groups in orbit.

speaker: Narrator
transcript: Among it were Quivers: disposable dispensers carrying the glide munitions of the opening Wave.

speaker: Narrator
transcript: A tug could spend weeks moving freight. There was time because the public deadline was still ahead.

speaker: Narrator
transcript: Wardens coordinated traffic in orbit. Far below them, Lanterns sensed and relayed from the stratosphere.

speaker: Narrator
transcript: Asteroids supplied metal. Compact fusion systems and high-grade seekers came from home.

speaker: Narrator
transcript: At Gamma, another assembly took shape around precision components drawn from a finite stock.

speaker: Narrator
transcript: At an observatory, two exposures might show a point of light changing position. The measurement could be sound while its meaning remained unclear.

speaker: Narrator
transcript: The scattered observations never became a warning governments could act on. The people comparing them had only pieces of the picture.

speaker: Narrator
transcript: Domesday sensors covered selected ground corridors. Much of the terrain remained unseen.

speaker: Narrator
transcript: In the final weeks, the workshops kept working as more of their output took its place above Earth.

speaker: Narrator
transcript: One dispenser had already been set aside for a demonstration. Its public announcement would come later.

speaker: Narrator
transcript: An inert Scythe would give observers a prediction to check. The event was still ahead.

speaker: Narrator
transcript: Nineteen months had passed since the Caravan arrived. On Earth, the first public word was still to come.

speaker: Narrator
transcript: The Company opened a public channel.

speaker: Company transmission
transcript: This transmission is of nonhuman origin.

speaker: Company transmission
transcript: Leave military equipment and military structures.
